recognize_zh: 視野中央的嗜中性球核分成 6 葉以上（下方一顆可數出約 6–7 葉），細胞體積也偏大，即為過度分葉嗜中性球 (hypersegmented neutrophil)，典型見於巨母紅血球性貧血 (megaloblastic anemia)。
features: Mature neutrophils with nuclei divided into six or more discrete lobes connected by thin chromatin filaments
Neutrophils appear slightly enlarged (macropolycytes) relative to surrounding red cells
Clumped mature chromatin; pale pink cytoplasm with fine neutrophilic granules, no toxic granulation or Döhle bodies
Red cells are normochromic, partly overlapping in stacked chains (thick-area/rouleaux-like arrangement)
Platelets present and scattered in the background
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows mature neutrophils with nuclear hypersegmentation; at least one neutrophil displays six or more nuclear lobes, and the neutrophils appear mildly enlarged. The cytoplasm contains normal fine granules without toxic changes. Red cells are overlapping in this field, limiting assessment of macro-ovalocytes, and platelets are present. Findings are consistent with neutrophil hypersegmentation, which should prompt evaluation for vitamin B12 or folate deficiency and exposure to antimetabolite drugs such as hydroxyurea or methotrexate.

ddx.vs: Normal neutrophils have 2–5 lobes, and hypersegmentation requires one cell with ≥6 lobes or >5% of neutrophils with 5 lobes.
The inherited form is a benign autosomal dominant trait with normal red cell indices and vitamin levels, so it is distinguished clinically and by family studies rather than morphology.
Pelger cells show the opposite change, with hyposegmented bilobed (pince-nez) or round nuclei.
MDS may show hypersegmentation but usually with hypogranular cytoplasm, pseudo-Pelger forms and cytopenias with normal B12/folate.
